items.weakness_text: Very poor writing and presentation, with missing basic punctuation.
Major contribution limited to a trivial 2-D convex quadratic case.
The overall paper is not well written.

Although this is a mathematical optimization paper, it should be better polished to improve readability. Symbols should be defined clearly, and more background information should be provided. Since this is an AI conference, it would also be beneficial to include experiments related to AI.
The scope of this work is extremely narrow.
The theoretically sound results are limited to the two-dimensional case, with claims for higher-dimensional extensions lacking formal justification.
Consequently, the connection to modern machine learning optimization problems is very weak, raising questions about whether this paper fits the scope of the intended venue.

The paper does not propose a fundamentally new optimization method but rather offers an alternative perspective on an existing algorithm, making it difficult to argue that it provides substantial new insight.
Overall presentation is not up to publication standards.
Numerous grammatical and stylistic issues (most notably, uncapitalized sentence beginnings).
Inconsistent notation without proper explanation or derivation (for example, the definition of $r$ in Equation 9).
Incorrect cross-references (such as “minimizing Eq.(3)” around line 034).
Use of unjustified or imprecise terminology (for instance, describing the system as “chaotic”, which is not supported by a rigorous definition or analysis).
